label: Reverse support between the two POTENCY_1 and privation analyses
summary: The November 13 reconstruction now has two result-backed directions at the existing generic statements. Given F (P iff capacity and lack of act), Q (privation iff lack of act on capable subjects) yields T (P iff capacity and privation), and T yields Q. The companion adoptedEquivalence substitutes the existing adopted function for every occurrence of P and uses AdoptedPotency.analysis, so only in that specialization can the equivalence omit F. Both argument records preserve the same freely supplied predicates and record F as their sense bridge. The proofs add conditional support choices. Because the only previous consumer of T and Q was their joint derivation of F, neither reverse rule gives an independent path into F. The fixed meanings and the prior conceptual warrant stand; the proof adds no observational or historical evidence. See docs/notes/potency-privation-support-investigation.md for the concrete First Way composition, fixed-point comparison, rival and revision tests.
blocker: Application to a power retained during exercise would need a different interpretation: at C and A that power can persist, whereas F excludes P there. For stage-relative privation establish that capacity implies due possession at that stage, or restrict Q. Reopen the present application if a consumer changes the subject, respect, act or evaluation context, or a capable instance violates Q in its broad sense.
